item.title: What is a Prompt Injection Attack? How It Works, Types, and Defensive Techniques Prompt injection is a systemic risk where LLMs follow malicious instructions hidden in inputs because they lack native trust boundaries. As models gain tools, memory, and autonomy, these attacks can trigger real data leaks and unauthorized actions unless controls exist outside the model.
item.description:
Author: Fergal Glynn
Date: January 05, 2026
Tags: ["Cybersecurity", "Artificial Intelligence", "Large Language Models", "Prompt Injection Attacks", "Data Security"]
Summary:
  • Prompt injection tricks language models into following malicious instructions.
  • These attacks exploit the lack of trust boundaries in LLMs.
  • They can cause data leaks and unauthorized actions.
  • Attacks can be direct or hidden in content.
  • Traditional injection differs as prompt injection targets instruction execution.
  • Defenses require controls outside the model itself.

item.title: 7 Ways to Secure LLMs Against Prompt Injections Prompt injection attacks exploit LLMs’ inability to separate trusted instructions from untrusted content. The only effective defense is layered security that limits impact when injections slip through.
item.description:
Author: Fergal Glynn
Date: January 05, 2026
Tags: ["AI Security", "Large Language Models", "Cybersecurity", "Prompt Injection Attacks", "Data Protection"]
Summary:
  • Prompt injections exploit LLMs' inability to separate trusted from untrusted instructions.
  • Attacks can be direct or indirect, with indirect being harder to detect.
  • Layered security is the only effective defense against these attacks.
  • Indirect injections hide in documents and data sources, tricking models silently.
  • Organizations must use adversarial testing and monitoring to secure LLMs.
  • Mindgard technology helps uncover hidden risks in LLM deployments.

item.title: Indirect Prompt Injections: 5 Real World Examples (and How to Prevent Them) Indirect prompt injections embed malicious instructions in trusted content, letting attackers hijack LLMs without direct user input. Effective prevention requires layered defenses, including input sanitization, strict instruction boundaries, least-privilege tools, and continuous testing.
item.description:
Author: Fergal Glynn
Date: January 05, 2026
Tags: ["Cybersecurity", "Artificial Intelligence", "Large Language Models", "Adversarial Attacks", "Data Protection"]
Summary:
  • Indirect prompt injections hide malicious instructions in trusted content.
  • They exploit AI systems without direct user input.
  • These attacks are harder to detect than direct injections.
  • Prevention needs layered defenses and continuous testing.
  • Examples include email footers, web pages, and internal knowledge bases.
  • Organizations must sanitize inputs and enforce strict controls.

item.title: Prompt Injection Attacks in ChatGPT: Vulnerabilities, Examples & Prevention Prompt injection attacks exploit LLMs’ lack of trust boundaries, allowing malicious instructions to override safeguards in ChatGPT, especially in RAG and agentic systems. Reducing risk requires layered defenses such as policy enforcement, prompt hardening, continuous testing, and output filtering.

item.title: Agent Security vs Agent Safety
item.description:
Author: Alessandro Pignati
Date: January 05, 2026
Tags: ["Artificial Intelligence", "AI Safety", "Cybersecurity", "Autonomous Systems", "Enterprise Technology"]
Summary:
  • Agentic AI is becoming common in enterprise applications.
  • Agent safety prevents unintentional harm by AI agents.
  • Agent security defends against intentional attacks by adversaries.
  • Safety focuses on alignment, robustness, and bias mitigation.
  • Security covers prompt injection, data theft, and unauthorized access.
  • Both are vital for trustworthy AI systems.
